A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same context-parroting study. Their text, equations, figures, references, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original forecasting experiments on 135 chaotic systems, inference-cost measurements, and embedding-dimension and scaling-law analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on broader scientific datasets, attractor reconstruction, observational noise, and sampling rates.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains nearest-motif matching, exclusion of the final D candidate motifs, and copying and repeating the matched continuation. Explicit Euclidean-distance wording and harmonized notation clarify the existing procedure rather than introduce a new component.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 adds von Karman vortex-flow data, QT Database ECG recordings, experimentally measured electronic circuits, and coupled Kuramoto oscillators beyond the retained low-dimensional dysts benchmark. Appendix E additionally evaluates noise-corrupted trajectories, substantially broadening the represented systems and input conditions.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate Chronos, Chronos Bolt, TimesFM-2.0, and Time-MoE. V2 extends this same comparator set to its additional experiments. Farmer-Sidorowich forecasting is newly discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 adds attractor KL divergence and correlation-dimension accuracy to the evaluation protocol. New scientific-task tables evaluate MAE and MSE at 50 steps, while sampling-rate experiments introduce 10 and 50 points per Lyapunov time alongside the retained 30-point setting. These substantially extend evaluation beyond the original forecasting metrics and protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix E systematically tests Gaussian-noise levels of 0.001, 0.01, and 0.1 and sampling granularities of 10, 30, and 50 points per Lyapunov time across five metrics. These add substantial robustness and sensitivity evidence; the original embedding-dimension and context-length analyses remain present.

E5.justification: V2 adds shaded variability bands to the existing MSE/MAE and scaling plots. Figure 10 explicitly specifies 100 trajectories per system for the embedding study, whereas v1 supplied only a general 20-trajectory protocol; an actual increase is not explicitly documented. The main comparisons retain 20 trajectories, and some new tabular ± quantities remain undefined.

E6.justification: Tables 1–13 and the attractor-reconstruction plots add substantial results; for example, Figure 8 reports correlation-dimension accuracy of 0.80 for Parrot and 0.85 for Chronos. Retained forecasting curves also change, and the inverse-scaling correlation is revised from 0.44 ± 0.08 in v1 Figure 7 to 0.51 ± 0.08 in v2 Figure 11. These are reported additions and revisions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix F.2 distinguishes input- and output-kernel dimensions where v1 C.2 supplied a single dimensionality statement. Appendix F.4 restricts the existing mixing/scaling discussion to stochastic series. The invariant-preservation proposition, derivation, and principal scaling arguments otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: V2 removes v1's categorical claim that foundation models fail to develop meaningful representations of physics, replacing it with the narrower conclusion that they underutilize context. It also elevates identifying shared failure modes into the stated contributions. This materially recalibrates the paper's central claims while retaining the baseline and scaling-law contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds local-trend continuation as an explanation for Chronos's short-context advantage, interprets sampling changes through time rescaling, and proposes benchmarks without nearly repeating motifs. The conclusion explicitly frames parroting as a diagnostic baseline rather than a replacement for foundation models. Mean-collapse explanations and the nonstationarity limitation already appeared in v1.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents zero-mean, unit-standard-deviation trajectory normalization, Gaussian-mixture KL estimation, and source and processing details for added datasets, including Reynolds number 900 and PCA modes for vortex-flow data. The normalization disclosure alone does not establish that preprocessing changed. No new code-access information is provided.

R1.justification: Eight references are added, covering transformer circuits, in-context learning, attractor evaluation, and the new datasets. Sections 3 and 5.2 now discuss Farmer-Sidorowich forecasting and acknowledge its related scaling law. The existing related-work themes and overall positioning remain recognizable.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract, contributions, and conclusion, expands embedding and metric explanations, and harmonizes notation across the theoretical appendix. Related-work subheadings become inline headings and several analyses receive separate appendices. Most existing exposition and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 introduces 13 tables, an attractor-KL violin plot, and a correlation-dimension comparison plot. Figure 2's VPT panel becomes a separate appendix figure, and the embedding and scaling-correlation figures move from the main text to appendices. Revised axes, captions, uncertainty displays, and table highlighting substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V1's broad conclusions rested on clean, low-dimensional simulations without direct attractor-reconstruction comparisons. V2 tests broader simulated and real systems, adds noise and sampling sensitivity checks, and directly evaluates attractor statistics. Together with the narrower physics-related claim, these changes substantially strengthen empirical support and claim calibration. Some new protocol details, uncertainty definitions, and explanations for revised plots remain incomplete.
